passage:
At ten, Kunal stumbled over a line in the reading and the class went quiet. He crossed his eyes and announced, in a booming voice, that the book had bitten his tongue. Everyone laughed, and Himani Ma'am shook her head with a small smile. Kunal laughed loudest, though his fingers tapped the desk rapidly.
Ten years later, Simran sat two rows behind him in a college lecture, thinking of the jokes he threw into every discussion. He was funny, sure of himself, and always in the middle of a group. After three chats at the canteen she had already pictured them travelling together and going to each other's family functions. One evening she asked about his plans after graduation. Kunal grinned. "Plans? I plan to have a very nice sandwich." The group laughed, and Simran laughed with them. Somewhere in the back of her mind she wondered if the easy confidence was the whole of him. She pushed the thought away and went on imagining the trip.

qa.q: What did Kunal claim had happened when he stumbled over the reading?
qa.a: He announced that the book had bitten his tongue.

qa.q: How does Simran's view of Kunal in college connect to his behaviour at ten?
qa.a: At ten Kunal crossed his eyes and joked when he was embarrassed, while his fingers tapped the desk. In college Simran sees only the funny, confident Kunal in the middle of a group and pictures them travelling together, so the person she imagines is partly the one she wishes for.

qa.q: What might Simran be feeling as she pushes the thought about his confidence away?
qa.a: She feels excited and infatuated, but also a small doubt she would rather not look at.

qa.q: What could Simran do to get to know Kunal better before imagining more?
qa.a: She could talk with him in quieter settings, notice how he handles stress and unfunny topics, and let the picture of him grow from what she really sees.

grounding: A child's joke covering embarrassment (3891) and a later classmate drawn to that same humour and confidence, filling in the rest with wishes (2998).
